newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH SHARES SEEN EXTENDING TWO-SESSION FALL.
newsitem.headline: POLISH SHARES SEEN EXTENDING TWO-SESSION FALL.

text.p: Polish shares were expected to fall for the third session running, signalled by Friday's stronger selling after price-fixing and at continuous trade.
Analysts saw the market flat or down this week after last week's 1.8-percent gain to 16,669.1 points, with the main WIG index staying between 16,000 and 17,000 points.
Some analysts said deeper falls were possible after the bourse's significant gains so far this year.

Analysts said NFI units could extend Friday's 2.7-percent fall after Thursday's news the finance ministry would scrap at 1998's start the corporate tax exemption the National Investment Funds (NFIs) enjoy on gains from selling firms from their portfolios.
